a5386.speech: “The IGAD notes the regrettable absence of the delegation of the Sudan Armed Forces despite the invitation and confirmation of attendance.”

a5386.speaker: Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a5386.speech: members raised concerns about “the escalation of the conflict, repeated violations of the various ceasefire agreements, and the spread of violence outside of [the capital] Khartoum” ; said the war had “assumed ethnic and religious dimensions” in Darfur and Kordofan and that this was going to deepen polarisation in the country ; says the war between the SAF and RSF has seen “escalation driven by external interference” ; “strongly [urged] the parties to immediately stop the violence and sign an unconditional and indefinite ceasefire through a cessation of hostilities agreement that shall be supported by an effective enforcement and monitoring mechanism”, emphasising that there will be no need for a military solution in Sudan.

a5386.speaker: IGAD Quartet (Kenya, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Djibouti)
a5386.speech: According to the Quartet, the SAF had earlier indicated that it would send an envoy but chose not to and gave no reasons.

a5386.speaker: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF)
a5386.speech: objected to having Kenya’s President William Ruto as the leader of the negotiation platform, accusing Ruto of being an ally of the rival RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo and instead wanting South Sudan to take charge.

a5386.speaker: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a5386.speech: According to Human Rights Watch (HRW), conflict in Sudan since independence from British rule in 1956 has been between the Arab-speaking Muslim elite from the northern Nile valley and non-Muslims who are economically, socially and politically marginalised.

a5594.speaker: A journalist (anonymous)
a5594.speech: "I got to know Mrs Coulibaly during my international missions to Bouake in the framework of sport. I saw in her a woman of great professional conscience. Welcoming, she remains very rigorous in her work. Sincerely, she is a real fighter."

a5594.speaker: Mrs Coulibaly Mariam Coulibaly, Governor of the Dioila Region (Mali)
a5594.speech: Declares: "The trust placed in me by the highest authorities to lead the Dioila region calls on my part for a challenge to meet the heavy responsibility that now falls to me, to administer the district in my charge in the best interests of the State and the population" ; commits to "doing everything possible to live up to expectations".

a5594.speaker: Mrs Coulibaly Mariam Coulibaly, Governor of the Dioila Region (Mali)
a5594.speech: Says she plans to multiply regular exchanges with elected officials, traditional authorities, civil society and the district's key stakeholders (young people, women, the elderly, people living with a disability) on major questions of national or regional interest, and intends to "ensure that the technical services of her region communicate periodically with their target publics for a better sharing of the objectives assigned to them".

a5594.speaker: Mrs Coulibaly Mariam Coulibaly, Governor of the Dioila Region (Mali)
a5594.speech: On the occasion of the 8 March celebration, addresses to her sisters "a message of courage and self-denial in participating in national construction as they already do so well in our towns and countryside".

a5757.speaker: Col Mahamane Elhadji Ousmane, Minister of Agriculture and Livestock of Niger
a5757.speech: Recalled in his launch speech that the Grand Irrigation Programme is an initiative of Brigadier General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP and Head of State, aimed at overhauling Niger's agricultural production system: “Without going back over the difficult moments we experienced following the unjust and unjustified sanctions imposed on our country in 2023, this overhaul will enable us to exploit our potential to produce locally what we need for our consumption, and even to export the surplus. On the strength of this commitment, the highest authorities have mobilised several actors around the PGI programme, so that our external dependence on basic food products finally ceases. We must absolutely seek by every means to boost our production in order to achieve the country’s food sovereignty.”

a5757.speaker: Col Mahamane Elhadji Ousmane, Minister of Agriculture and Livestock of Niger
a5757.speech: Indicated that the works consist of the rehabilitation and development of the hydro-agricultural perimeters of Tiguirwitt 1, 2 and 3 in the rural commune of Ingall, and will also concern new developments studied by the Directorate General of Rural Engineering at the sites of Dirkou (48 hectares), Tabakat/Teguidanadar (120 hectares), Teguidan Teguet (96 hectares) and Taslim (48 hectares)

a5757.speaker: Col Mahamane Elhadji Ousmane, Minister of Agriculture and Livestock of Niger
a5757.speech: Issued a call for the mobilisation of everyone, particularly young people and women, for the success of the programme: “To achieve the targeted results and meet this considerable challenge, the massive support of the entire population of the Agadez region, particularly the youth, is indispensable, since they constitute the bulk of the majority segment of the Nigerien population and can develop our potential and develop our significant land resources throughout the country in order to considerably reduce imports of food products.”

a5757.speaker: Col Mahamane Elhadji Ousmane, Minister of Agriculture and Livestock of Niger
a5757.speech: Expressed satisfaction that the PGI is on a sure footing and responds to the region’s priority needs: “Our ambition of large-scale production through the PGI requires us to implement special measures. That is to say, financing from the State’s own resources and execution of the works by national companies, notably the Office of Hydro-Agricultural Developments (ONAHA)” ; stressed that a multi-year plan contract for 2024-2027 has been signed with ONAHA for new developments and the rehabilitation of existing irrigated perimeters in Niger

a5757.speaker: Brigadier General Ibra Boulama Issa, Governor of the Agadez region
a5757.speech: Expressed his gratitude and joy at the launch of the Grand Irrigation Programme: “This day will certainly mark the history of the Agadez region because this moment gives concrete form to the commitments we made a few months ago to our people in the framework of food sovereignty, to which the highest authorities attach great value. I must say that the implementation of the Grand Irrigation Programme has accelerated very well (...) looking at the ground covered in so little time, notably the various works already launched in four (4) regions, we can only congratulate you on the work accomplished. We are delighted to see that this challenge is being met by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, and as you know, the potential of the Agadez region is very considerable, with nearly 25% of Niger’s irrigable land.”

a5757.speaker: Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Ingall and the Vice-President of the Regional Youth Council
Idrissa Ibrahim, Vice-President of the National Youth Council
a5757.speech: Reiterated his organisation’s commitment to continue raising awareness among young people for the success of the programme

a5759.speaker: Lot Ndamanomhata, NamWater spokesperson
a5759.speech: “This is a 16% increase from the N$2.1 billion recorded in June 2024, which poses a serious threat to the long-term sustainability of water supply in Namibia” (in a statement issued on Monday) ; “The continued failure to settle water bills severely affects NamWater’s ability to operate effectively. Unlike profit-driven businesses, NamWater relies solely on revenue from water sales to maintain operations, infrastructure and service delivery” ; emphasised that as a 100% state-owned enterprise NamWater does not receive any subsidies from its shareholder and has not implemented any tariff adjustments over the past five years ; “Revenue collections fluctuate based on water consumption and payment compliance. The growing debt burden – currently at N$2.4 billion – poses a significant risk to sustainable revenue collection. Meanwhile, the cost of providing water – particularly energy costs – continues to rise.”

a5759.speaker: Lot Ndamanomhata, NamWater spokesperson
a5759.speech: Urged debtors to settle their outstanding balances: “To prevent potential water interruptions and ensure continued water supply, NamWater requests local authorities, state institutions, industries and private consumers to settle their outstanding accounts” ; noted that if the situation does not improve, “NamWater may have no choice but to implement stricter measures to recover outstanding payments” ; said some residents have expressed concern that they pay their water bills to local authorities but these payments are not forwarded to NamWater, and that accountability in revenue management remains critical and must be strengthened, particularly at local authorities ; “Water is a fundamental necessity, and without timely payments, the ability to provide this essential resource will be severely compromised.”

a5759.speaker: Lot Ndamanomhata, NamWater spokesperson
a5759.speech: Explained that NamWater is a bulk water supplier that relies on revenue from water sales to maintain operations, upgrade infrastructure and expand access: “Without debt recovery, investments in ageing infrastructure will be delayed, jeopardising reliable water supply” ; added that while the Namibian government, largely through NamWater, currently provides water access to 87% of the population, further expansion into underserved communities is at risk due to the financial strain caused by unpaid debts ; “Non-payment becomes unsustainable – as seen with outstanding debts exceeding N$2.4 billion. NamWater is forced to take measures to recover funds and ensure service continuity. The goal is to ensure that water supply remains uninterrupted while maintaining financial sustainability.”

a5816.speaker: Health experts (Gatefield Health Summit 2025 fireside chat)
a5816.speech: Have urged the Nigerian government to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation and prioritise safety-based funding as a pathway to building a resilient and self-sustaining health system.

a5816.speaker: Shola Dele-Olowu, Director of Regional Initiatives at AMP Health
a5816.speech: Said Nigeria must shift from external aid to domestic financing to secure its health system’s future ; described the current global funding decline as a reminder that donor nations will prioritise their citizens first during crises ; "We cannot continue to depend on external funding to finance our essential services. The transition shock from donor withdrawal has given way to opportunity, and innovation is usually born out of crisis," she said ; cited Ghana’s approach after the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) exit, noting that the country raised taxes on sugar and leveraged its gold sector to fund maternal and child health programmes ; according to her, Nigeria must treat this period as a wake-up call to improve fiscal accountability and demonstrate efficient use of available resources.

a5816.speaker: Shola Dele-Olowu, Director of Regional Initiatives at AMP Health
a5816.speech: Highlighted that innovation should not always be about large-scale projects, citing Guyana, a South American country, where health workers now access malaria treatment guidelines through WhatsApp-based AI chatbots, significantly reducing the cost of printing bulky manuals ; emphasised the importance of process innovations, small but effective adjustments that reduce costs, improve efficiency, and strengthen health system resilience.

a5816.speaker: Shola Dele-Olowu, Director of Regional Initiatives at AMP Health
a5816.speech: Stressed that human capacity is central to system sustainability, urging long-term investment in health workers and programme staff rather than focusing solely on short-term outputs.

a5816.speaker: Omokhudu Idogho, Managing Director, Society for Family Health (SFH) (represented by Anthony Nwala)
a5816.speech: Said Nigeria’s health sector must deliberately mobilise resources internally and use data to guide spending and policy decisions ; noted that the scale-back of donor support by agencies led to SFH establishing subsidiary organisations to diversify income streams and provide technical assistance to governments at multiple levels ; "We must be intentional about internal resource mobilisation. Each time we respond to a crisis, it should become a practice, not an act of desperation," he said ; emphasised the need for self-honesty in government financial planning, urging transparent and deliberate use of funds ; highlighted that resilience depends on understanding gaps, analysing data, and channelling resources strategically rather than following traditional patterns or spending simply because it has been done that way before.

a5816.speaker: Omokhudu Idogho, Managing Director, Society for Family Health (SFH) (represented by Anthony Nwala)
a5816.speech: Said community ownership is central to health system resilience ; cited SFH’s partnerships with transport unions in northern Nigeria to provide emergency transport services for pregnant women, which contributed to a reduction in maternal mortality ; referenced initiatives in Delta State, where Nigerians in the diaspora sponsor indigent households through the state’s Contributory Health Scheme, helping to reduce out-of-pocket health expenditure ; stressed that existing community structures, including traditional leaders, local associations, and volunteer health workers, should be leveraged for awareness creation, health promotion, and service delivery ; noted that resilience is about people, not just programmes or funding, and that communities must be empowered to take ownership of health interventions to ensure long-term sustainability.

a5849.speaker: U.S. Government (statement marking World Malaria Day)
a5849.speech: Celebrates the advances Mozambique has made in preventing and treating malaria and recommits to continue supporting Mozambique's efforts at eliminating the disease, noting it has invested more than $416 million since 2007 and provides more than $500 million in annual assistance to Mozambique.

a5849.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, U.S. Ambassador to Mozambique
a5849.speech: "The United States is proud of its more than 15-year partnership with Mozambique to combat malaria. Investments we make together with the goal of ending malaria-related deaths not only save lives now, but also help prepare to respond to future health threats."

a5849.speaker: World Health Organization
a5849.speech: Reported more than 600,000 people died of malaria in 2020, 96 percent of which were in Africa.

a5861.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia
a5861.speech: Announced the organization of a strategic retreat to address emerging challenges within the country's global development framework, in response to a significant reduction in assistance from USAID ; says it remains committed to working closely with all stakeholders to secure sustainable and well-coordinated support for the country's development agenda.

a5861.speaker: Dephue Zuo, Deputy Minister of Finance of Liberia
a5861.speech: Disclosed that the retreat will serve as a platform to evaluate the progress of Liberia's development agenda, known as the AAID, which was unveiled by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai in January of this year ; According to Deputy Minister Zuo, the AAID was launched with a clear roadmap for resource allocation, drawing support from international donors, the private sector, the diaspora community, and domestic revenues ; "This situation calls for urgent steps to assess where we are and how best we can align our priorities with available donor support to repurpose existing funding."

a5861.speaker: Christian Umutoni, United Nations Resident Coordinator, and the Swedish Ambassador to Liberia
a5861.speech: Welcomed the government's initiative and praised the planned retreat as an opportunity to strengthen cooperation and mutual accountability, noting that inclusive dialogue is essential to addressing current development challenges ; expressed optimism about the retreat, describing it as a timely and necessary step to encourage national ownership and coordination in development planning.

a5875.speaker: Zhuo Ruisheng, Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti
a5875.speech: "Today, the fight against the new coronavirus epidemic is the most important and most urgent task of the Chinese government." ; Said that under the personal leadership of President Xi Jinping an ad hoc anti-epidemic group chaired by Premier Li Keqiang was set up and the strictest prevention and control measures adopted: scientific studies traced the virus within a week, Wuhan (11 million inhabitants) was quarantined with air, rail, road and river links closed, some 70 medical teams totalling over 8,000 people were sent in, two dedicated hospitals with more than 2,000 beds were urgently built, provinces triggered the level I public health emergency plan, and China engaged in international cooperation by informing the WHO in a timely manner and immediately sharing the virus genome sequence.

a5875.speaker: Zhuo Ruisheng, Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti
a5875.speech: Said that while the epidemic situation remains serious, the measures adopted by China are beginning to produce positive effects: 657 cases have been cured and the outbreak has been effectively contained nationally and internationally, showing that "this new coronavirus is preventable, controllable and curable"; noted that of 20,623 confirmed cases worldwide up to 3 February, 20,471 (99.26%) were in China and only one of the 427 deaths occurred in an Asian country other than China.

a5875.speaker: Zhuo Ruisheng, Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti
a5875.speech: On airlines suspending flights to China, said "these are rather economic decisions" and noted the WHO had declared there was no reason to take measures that unnecessarily disrupt international travel and trade; added that "the only thing we have to fear is fear itself. The greatest enemy in our fight is not the virus, but panic."

a5875.speaker: Zhuo Ruisheng, Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti
a5875.speech: On the WHO's declaration of a public health emergency of international concern, said it is "a technical decision made by the WHO in conformity with the International Health Regulations" falling within the Organization's competence, that many of China's prevention and control measures "go well beyond the requirements of the International Health Regulations", and that China will continue to work with the WHO and other countries to respond to the outbreak.

a5875.speaker: Zhuo Ruisheng, Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti
a5875.speech: On the economy, said the epidemic "could have temporary consequences for the Chinese economy, but the long-term impact should not be exaggerated"; said the resilience of an economy with 1.4 billion consumers cannot be underestimated, that impacts on tourism, leisure, catering, trade and foreign direct investment will be short-lived, and that the epidemic even benefits innovative sectors such as e-commerce, the Internet, 5G and artificial intelligence.

a5875.speaker: Zhuo Ruisheng, Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti
a5875.speech: On the risk to Djibouti, said the Chinese Embassy in Djibouti immediately recommended that recently arrived Chinese citizens observe home isolation and reduce movement in public places; noted only about twenty Chinese citizens had come from China since January, that the crew of a Chinese navy frigate did not leave the quay while berthed in Djibouti, that there is no confirmed or suspected case in Djibouti, and that "thanks to the combined efforts of China and Djibouti, this epidemic will not constitute a serious threat to Djibouti", while warning to remain vigilant against panic-provoking rumours.

a5875.speaker: Zhuo Ruisheng, Chinese Ambassador to Djibouti
a5875.speech: In his message to the Djiboutian population, said China "treats its own citizens and foreigners on an equal footing, including the Djiboutian community residing in China", that no other country could take such measures in so short a time, that the leadership of the Communist Party with Xi Jinping at its core and the socialist system are an incomparable asset, and thanked the Djiboutian people and government for their friendship and constant support for China.

a5875.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the WHO
a5875.speech: Said the speed with which China detected the outbreak, isolated the virus and communicated the genome to the WHO and the world is particularly impressive and that China's commitment to transparency is no less so; said China has set a new standard in outbreak response and that its measures "command respect and deserve the recognition of the whole world"; attributed the very low number of exported cases and deaths outside China in large part to the unprecedented measures taken by the Chinese authorities.

a5875.speaker: Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the WHO
a5875.speech: Declared on 30 January that the new coronavirus outbreak constituted a public health emergency of international concern, saying the declaration was not mainly due to what is happening in China but to what is happening in other countries, notably the possibility that the virus spreads to countries with more fragile health systems; stressed it was not a mark of distrust towards China and recommended not limiting trade and travel to China.

a5875.speaker: Djiboutian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI)
a5875.speech: Said that Djiboutian students and citizens in Wuhan and other Chinese cities are all doing well and in good health at present.

a5890.speaker: Arthur Lichenya, Card (Churches Action in Relief and Development) programmes manager
a5890.speech: Said the money is for beneficiaries to buy maize for three months ; “This intervention is under the El Nino response project, which is being implemented by a consortium of partners. We rolled out the initiative because of the El Nino weather phenomenon which affected crop yield in the 2024/25 growing season. Nsanje is one of the districts that was affected.”

a5890.speaker: Fyawupi Mwafongo, Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma) deputy director of disaster response
a5890.speech: Said they are satisfied with the project’s interventions ; “We have a national resilience strategy to break the cycle of food insecurity. One of the initiatives is moving from over reliance on relief items to irrigation farming. We have started reaching out to partners to help in revamping irrigation schemes.”

a5890.speaker: Burnnet Khulumbo, Care Malawi humanitarian assistance manager
a5890.speech: Encouraged beneficiaries to diversify their crop production.

a5890.speaker: Rose Elias, beneficiary from group village head Dick
a5890.speech: Said the dry spells affected her crops ; “I had nothing to eat until I received the money to buy food.”

a5992.speaker: Bihi Imaan Egeh, Somali Finance Minister
a5992.speech: Told lawmakers on Wednesday that the Somali government must take greater financial responsibility for national priorities, including security, after a shift in the global aid landscape; urged Somali citizens to pay their taxes to help offset funding shortfalls and support economic growth ; “We must work together to accelerate tax reforms, manage foreign aid more effectively, and optimize available resources” ; “This funding reduction is not limited to the United States; it is a global trend.”

a5992.speaker: Bihi Imaan Egeh, Somali Finance Minister (on the Danab brigade)
a5992.speech: Further informed Parliament that the U.S. decision has directly affected the Danab forces, forcing the government to reallocate resources and establish a new budget to cover their salaries.

a6172.speaker: White House official (unnamed)
a6172.speech: Said on Wednesday that U.S. President Donald Trump will host leaders from five African nations – Gabon, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mauritania and Senegal – in Washington for a discussion and lunch at the White House on July 9 to discuss “commercial opportunities”: “President Trump believes that African countries offer incredible commercial opportunities which benefit both the American people and our African partners.”

a6172.speaker: Africa Intelligence and Semafor
a6172.speech: Reported earlier that the Trump administration would hold a summit for the five countries in Washington from July 9-11.

a6172.speaker: Trump administration
a6172.speech: Says it wants to focus on trade and investment and to drive mutual prosperity, after axing swaths of U.S. foreign aid for Africa as part of a plan to curb spending it considers wasteful and not aligned with Trump’s “America First” policies.

a6172.speaker: Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State
a6172.speech: Said on Tuesday the U.S. was abandoning what he called a charity-based foreign aid model and will favor those nations that demonstrate “both the ability and willingness to help themselves.”

a6172.speaker: Troy Fitrel, African Affairs senior bureau official
a6172.speech: Said in May that U.S. envoys in Africa will be rated on commercial deals struck, describing it as the new strategy for support on the continent.

a6349.speaker: United States government
a6349.speech: Announced the award of a $450,000 grant to support emergency relief efforts following tropical cyclone Chido, which devastated some regions of Mozambique last December.

a6349.speaker: Peter H. Vrooman, United States Ambassador (to Mozambique)
a6349.speech: Stressed the importance of rapid action to help the cyclone's victims. “The United States government recognises the immense challenges facing the affected populations and wishes to reaffirm our solidarity. Our aid will provide vital assistance to the people most affected by the cyclone, helping to reduce human suffering and to support recovery efforts,” Mr. Vrooman said.

a6452.speaker: Patty Murray, US Senator and head of the Senate delegation
a6452.speech: “We had an excellent conversation with the Prime Minister about values we share”, with Cape Verde being “a brilliant example of the importance of democracy” ; considered, at the start of a tour of five countries in Africa, that it is “important to continue cooperation” with the archipelago.

a6452.speaker: Chris Coons, US Senator
a6452.speech: Said he hoped the support would materialise, making Cape Verde the first country to benefit from three MCC support packages ; noted that ECOWAS “has witnessed many coups d'etat” in the past year, making it important “that there be a stable democracy” such as that of Cape Verde.

a6629.speaker: Adriano Maleiane, then Mozambican Prime Minister
a6629.speech: Shortly before Christmas, announced that the government does not have enough money to pay the bonus. He claimed that the state budget only contained enough money to pay the December wage bill, and to solve “some specific questions, particularly with regard to education”.

a6629.speaker: Trade unions representing public service workers
a6629.speech: Immediately threatened to go on strike.

a6629.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, Mozambican Minister/government spokesperson
a6629.speech: Said the 13th month would be paid, but only in February; for most of the public service only 50 per cent of the bonus will be paid, but for state pensioners the figure rises to 100 per cent ; told reporters that so far about 50 per cent of all workers of the public administration have received their 13th month. He believed that the rest will be paid by next Tuesday, assuming that the state institutions they work for submit the relevant wage sheets on time ; was confident that the missing wage sheets would arrive, and payment would then be made.

a6629.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, Mozambican Minister/government spokesperson
a6629.speech: Asked about the teachers who are refusing to mark the end-of-year examination papers until they are paid for the overtime they have worked, said the government is still in dialogue with the teachers. He stressed that payment of teachers’ basic wages is up-to-date, and the only question is when the overtime will be paid ; added that, in the first 100 days of the new government, overtime should be held to a minimum, and that as from now overtime worked by teachers must be paid the following month, to avoid the accumulation of debts to the teachers.

a6629.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, Mozambican Minister/government spokesperson
a6629.speech: Said the government is speaking with representatives of the United States government in an attempt to reverse the decision to suspend foreign aid; said it would have a strong impact on Mozambique, even though life-saving aid in the health sector is supposed to be exempt ; called for those affected by the cuts to stay calm, and assured them that the government is attempting to reverse or mitigate the effects and was also seeking to mobilise alternative sources of funding ; added that the government will also “redefine priorities and make the best use of existing resources” to minimise the impact of the cuts on essential services ; “The sudden withdrawal of this support to some extent compromises efficiency in the implementation of these programmes” ; noted that Mozambique has a ratio of 18.5 health professionals per each 10,000 inhabitants against a WHO target of 45: “We are a very long way from this target”, he said, “and this suspension decreed by the United States will impose an enormous challenge for us meeting the target”.

a6629.speaker: Trump administration
a6629.speech: Announced that the suspension is initially only for 90 days.

a6629.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, Mozambican Minister/government spokesperson
a6629.speech: Promised that from now on the government will give regular, weekly press briefings, meeting with journalists every Friday.

a6637.speaker: All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) (statement issued February 12 by General Secretary Rev. Dr. Fidon Mwombeki)
a6637.speech: Is requesting its members to indulge in “ceaseless prayers for God’s intervention in the disturbing situation in the eastern part of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and bring enduring peace to the region” ; emphasises: “It is no news that our brothers and sisters are in desperate and distressing situation that require our prayerful accompaniment and solidarity” ; invites members to pray for the DRC authorities to continue to apply wisdom and resources to provide protection for citizens and distressed civilians, for the authorities to take concrete steps to address the drivers of conflict and provide emergency relief, for the processes that will follow the resolutions of the joint EAC and SADC Heads of States Summit, and for all stakeholders in the DRC conflict to be sensitive to the plights of the victims and work towards restoration of peace ; “May the God of life, love, peace and comfort intervene in this situation!”

a6637.speaker: Deutsche Welle (report)
a6637.speech: Reported that despite a regional summit held on Saturday in Tanzania — co-chaired by SADC’s chairperson, Zimbabwe President Emerson Mnangagwa and EAC’s William Ruto, President of Kenya to stop fighting in the eastern DRC — “there is no resolution in sight” ; “prospects for peace seem far from certain, even though Rwandan President Paul Kagame and his DRC counterpart Felix Tshisekedi took part in the summit, albeit with Tshisekedi joining via video link” ; further reports that by the end of January, the Rwanda-supported M23 rebel group claimed control of Goma, the capital of the North Kivu province in the eastern DRC, and ordered government troops to surrender.

a6637.speaker: SADC-EAC joint Heads of State Summit (directives and final statement)
a6637.speech: Chiefs of Defence Forces were directed to meet within 5 days and provide technical direction on immediate and unconditional ceasefire and cessation of hostilities in the Eastern DRC; further directed the SADC-EAC Chiefs of Defence Forces to oversee the provision of humanitarian assistance including repatriation of the deceased and evacuation of the injured, to develop a securitisation plan for Goma and surrounding areas, and to oversee the opening of main supply routes and monitor the immediate reopening of Goma Airport ; the summit’s final statement affirmed support for the DRC’s territorial integrity and urged the opening of humanitarian corridors to evacuate the dead and wounded, but made no explicit reference to Rwanda or its part in the conflict ; the Heads of State reaffirmed their “solidarity and unwavering commitment to continue supporting the DRC in its pursuit of safeguarding its independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity as well as sustainable peace security and development”; also calling for cessation of hostilities and an immediate ceasefire, restoration of essential utilities and supply lines, and peaceful resolution through the merged Luanda/Nairobi process.

a6637.speaker: United Nations report (last year)
a6637.speech: Said Rwanda maintained around 4,000 troops in the DRC and had de facto control of the M23.

a6637.speaker: Paul Kagame, Rwandan President
a6637.speech: Afterwards, said his country will not be silent if its security is threatened, and criticised Tshisekedi for shifting blame for the conflict.

a6637.speaker: Rwanda (government)
a6637.speech: Denies it supports the M23, or that it has troops in the DRC.

a6637.speaker: Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, DRC Foreign Minister
a6637.speech: Appearing before an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council in New York, asked what international law Rwanda would still need to violate for global agencies to respond with concrete measures.

a6637.speaker: UN Security Council (statement)
a6637.speech: The statement released at the UN Security Council’s meeting merely called for the removal of “external forces,” without specifically naming Rwanda.

a6637.speaker: Representative of the UN Organisation Stabilisation Mission in the DRC (MONUSCO)
a6637.speech: Said that last week, at least 2,900 people had been killed as the M23 militia claimed control of Goma on January 27 and in the immediate aftermath.

a6637.speaker: Volker Turk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a6637.speech: “If nothing is done, the worst could be yet to come,” quoted as saying in Geneva on Friday.

a6639.speaker: Zimbabwean government (announcement)
a6639.speech: Announced that it has sufficient stock of antiretroviral (ARV) drugs to last for the next six months, coupled with ongoing procurement efforts to secure supplies through year-end.

a6716.speaker: Prof. Charlemagne Ouédraogo, Minister of Health of Burkina Faso
a6716.speech: Defended the two bills (the Bobo-Dioulasso radiotherapy centre project and the IDA financing agreement) before the National Assembly.

a6716.speaker: Deputies of the National Assembly of Burkina Faso
a6716.speech: Asked questions about the difficulties affecting the construction of health facilities and of certain referral hospitals such as the Yalgado-Ouédraogo University Hospital Centre; they also wanted to know the causes of cancers, their mode of treatment, the slowness in carrying out the works, etc.

a6721.speaker: Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt (company statement)
a6721.speech: Said on Thursday that it will start producing lithium sulphate during the first quarter of 2026 from its new $400 million plant in Zimbabwe.

a6721.speaker: Huayou executive (unnamed), speaking during a tour of the operation
a6721.speech: Said the newly completed plant at Huayou’s wholly owned Prospect Lithium Zimbabwe’s Arcadia mine has capacity to exceed 50,000 metric tons of lithium sulphate annually.

a6721.speaker: Henry Zhu, general manager of Prospect Lithium Zimbabwe
a6721.speech: “We will start the first production from the beginning of next year” ; “The quantity of the lithium sulphate should be more than 60,000 metric tons, but it will depend on the configuration of the plant, because it is brand new.”

a6721.speaker: Sinomine
a6721.speech: Has also announced plans to build a $500 million lithium sulphate plant at its Bikita mine in Zimbabwe.

a6776.speaker: Federal Executive Council (FEC) of Nigeria
a6776.speech: Announced, after its meeting on Monday, approval of a N4.8 billion fund for the procurement of 150,000 HIV treatment packs, ensuring continuous care for those living with the virus as part of efforts to strengthen domestic funding for HIV treatment.

a6776.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6776.speech: Emphasised the importance of sustaining HIV treatment efforts, particularly as international aid dynamics shift, noting that while global partners have played a crucial role in providing treatment support, the federal government is now taking deliberate steps to invest in life-saving interventions for People Living with HIV (PLHIV) in Nigeria: "This is an important signal that the federal government is committed to ensuring that life-saving treatments remain accessible, despite the changing dynamics in external support."

a6776.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6776.speech: Reassured stakeholders that the Nigerian government is proactively developing a transition and sustainability plan to address potential funding shortfalls, and disclosed that the FEC discussed the implications of US policy changes on health programmes, particularly those addressing HIV, tuberculosis and malaria: "In light of the US government's ongoing 90-day review of its development assistance policies, we have set up a committee comprising the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Defense, Ministry of Environment, and the Governors' Forum to develop a transition and sustainability plan" ; "This is to ensure that Nigerians receiving treatment do not face disruptions."

a6776.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6776.speech: Acknowledged the significant contributions made by the US over the past two decades but stressed that Nigeria is preparing to reduce its reliance on foreign aid: "While we greatly appreciate the contributions of the US government over the last 20 years and look forward to continued collaboration, Nigeria under President Bola Tinubu is focused on transforming the health sector through national systems and domestic financing." Said the goal is to ensure that no patient currently receiving treatment is left without care.

a6803.speaker: Eli Cohen, Israeli Minister of Energy
a6803.speech: Ordered the immediate suspension of the electricity supply to the Gaza Strip and assured that he will use every means at his disposal to secure the return of all Israeli hostages; the announced power cut covers the only electricity line between Israel and Gaza, through which power is supplied to the main water desalination plant serving more than 600,000 people.

a6803.speaker: Hamas, Palestinian group
a6803.speech: Accuses the Tel Aviv government of promoting an escalation of the genocide in its territory.

a6803.speaker: Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (note released by the international media)
a6803.speech: Vehemently condemned the measure, accusing the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of intending to promote an escalation of the genocide in the Gaza Strip; criticises the failure to implement UN resolutions and the provisional orders of the International Court of Justice for allegedly encouraging Israeli incursions against the Palestinians.

a6828.speaker: Grant Phillipo, US Embassy Public Affairs Officer
a6828.speech: Said American support to Malawi has been substantial, with $1.8 billion dedicated to HIV programmes since 2004, and $687 million in humanitarian assistance between 2000 and 2023: “Our partnership has extended beyond financial support to include conservation efforts, climate action initiatives and environmental protection. USaid projects have created 300,000 short-term jobs and facilitated the planting of 20 million trees.”

a6828.speaker: Bertha Chikadza, President of the Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a6828.speech: Said the timing of the aid freeze coincides with Malawi’s efforts to rebuild its economy amid rising inflation and foreign exchange shortages, potentially complicating the country’s recovery efforts: “The suspension threatens critical sectors dependent on US funding. Beyond the immediate impact on planned projects, this creates uncertainty in our development planning.”

a6828.speaker: Williams Banda, spokesperson for the Ministry of Finance (Malawi)
a6828.speech: Acknowledged the significance of US support while declining to make a detailed comment on the suspension’s implications: “The existing cordial relationship with the US remains valuable to us.”

a6939.speaker: Council of Ministers of Mali (communiqué CM N°2025-16/SGG, signed by Birama Coulibaly, Secretary General of the Government)
a6939.speech: States that the Council of Ministers met in ordinary session on Wednesday 16 April 2025 in its deliberations room at the Koulouba Palace, under the chairmanship of General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State, and that after examining the items on the agenda the Council adopted draft texts, made appointments, and heard communications.

a6939.speaker: Minister of the Economy and Finance of Mali
a6939.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft decree approving the contract for the purchase of 21,543 tonnes of fertiliser and its delivery to Bamako for the benefit of the beneficiaries of the Agricultural Productivity and Diversification Development Project in the Arid and Semi-arid Zones of Mali - concluded between the Government of the Republic of Mali and Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP-AFRICA) for 9 billion 838 million 580 thousand CFA francs excluding VAT with a 45-day execution period, the execution of which will improve agricultural productivity and strengthen the resilience of rural households in the project's intervention areas; and a draft decree approving the contract for the air transport of pilgrims of the governmental Hajj channel and their luggage for Hajj 2025, concluded with the EGYPTAIR KALIS VOYAGES-SARL grouping for 2 billion 62 million 500 thousand CFA francs with a one-month execution period, allowing those pilgrims to fulfil their religious duty in the best conditions.

a6939.speaker: Minister of Mines of Mali
a6939.speech: On his report, the Council of Ministers adopted a draft decree authorising the transfer to Les Mines de Lithium de Bougouni-S.A. of the large lithium mine exploitation permit awarded to Future Minerals-SARL at Foulaboula, in the Bougouni Circle, Bougouni Region; exploration work carried out by the company at Foulaboula led to the discovery of a lithium deposit with reserves estimated at 21.31 million tonnes at a grade of 1.11% lithium oxide, exploitable by the conventional open-pit method over 10 years.

a6939.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali
a6939.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of the 4th edition of the Antalya Diplomacy Forum in Turkiye, in which he participated from 11 to 13 April 2025 at the invitation of the Turkish Foreign Minister; the meeting allowed the dissemination of the Transition's major messages in the fields of Defence and Security as well as on geopolitical issues, and in the margins of the forum he held bilateral talks with his counterparts from Turkiye, Sudan and Venezuela and with the UN High Representative for the Alliance of Civilizations.

a6939.speaker: Foreign ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES)
a6939.speech: During the panel entitled "The Sahel: the future of regional integration", the ministers in charge of Foreign Affairs of the Confederation of Sahel States provided the elements necessary for an objective understanding of the situation in the Sahel and of the efforts undertaken by the Confederation in the framework of the fight against terrorism; they also communicated on the conditions for joining the AES Confederation, the establishment of the confederal levy, and cooperation between the AES Confederation and ECOWAS.

a6939.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
a6939.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of Mali's participation in the High-Level Forum "Dakar+10", held from 7 to 9 April 2025 in Dakar, Senegal, whose objective was to take stock of the 2013 Dakar Declaration on irrigation and to propose new approaches for the development of resilient and sustainable irrigation systems and for food and nutritional sovereignty in the Sahel.

a6939.speaker: Participants of the "Dakar+10" High-Level Forum
a6939.speech: At the close of proceedings, the participants validated the new regional irrigation strategy for the Sahel and formulated recommendations for stakeholders, notably: the alignment of technical and financial partners' funding with the political priorities of the States; the reduction of food imports through the development of irrigation; and the scaling up of irrigation solutions developed and documented under the Regional Support Project for the Sahel Irrigation Initiative.

a6939.speaker: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a6939.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the holding of the 2nd meeting of the ministers in charge of Industry and Trade of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), held on 10 April 2025 in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, under the chairmanship of the Burkinabe Prime Minister, Head of Government, following their first meeting on 19 October 2024 in Bamako.

a6939.speaker: Ministers in charge of Industry and Trade of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES)
a6939.speech: At the close of proceedings, the ministers adopted several key documents to accelerate regional integration, notably the timetable for implementing the recommendations of the Bamako meeting, and took note of the conclusions of the work of the Confederation's private-sector organisations; faced with security stakes and development challenges, they committed to implementing priority actions, to harmonising import, export and transit procedures for two-wheeled vehicles within the confederal space and to strengthening public-private dialogue, and further committed to developing joint projects such as the construction of a confederal power plant and of a railway linking the member states' capitals and certain transit countries.

a6939.speaker: Minister of Handicrafts, Culture, the Hotel Industry and Tourism of Mali
a6939.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the concept of the "Maliden Kura Talent Incubators", an initiative aiming to train and promote young Malian talents as part of the implementation of the Culture Mali 2025 project, comprising a four-month professionalisation process and support to fund the incubated talents' projects, with 25 young beneficiaries per cohort selected through a call for applications in different artistic and cultural fields; and of the organisation of the Triangle du Balafon International Festival, initiated in 2004 by Burkina Faso, Cote d'Ivoire and Mali, whose 9th edition, under the theme "The Balafon, symbol of social transformation in a new sovereign space", is scheduled for October 2025 in the Sikasso Region and will also be an opportunity to strengthen cohesion among the peoples of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES).

a6939.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a6939.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the country's epidemiological situation, marked notably by an increase in the number of confirmed dengue cases compared with the previous week.

a6939.speaker: General of the Army Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State
a6939.speech: Called on the population to strictly respect measures for the prevention of and fight against diseases.

a7000.speaker: S&P Global Ratings (credit rating report)
a7000.speech: Affirmed its 'SD/SD' (selective default) long-term and short-term local currency sovereign credit ratings on Mozambique and its 'CCC+/C' long-term and short-term foreign currency sovereign credit ratings; the outlook on the FC rating remains negative. "Amid these constrained liquidity conditions, we consider ongoing domestic debt switch auctions distressed and tantamount to default, because we do not think the government would otherwise be able to honor these obligations on time and in full. We also understand there have been ongoing delays in payments on Mozambique's local currency debt, in some cases for several months." ; "The negative outlook reflects ongoing external financing constraints and risks of further delays to planned gas projects in and foreign aid to the country, which could adversely affect Mozambique's ability to stay current on its foreign currency debt obligations in the next 12-24 months."

a7000.speaker: S&P Global Ratings (credit rating report)
a7000.speech: Said "the suspension of U.S.-related funding (especially from the U.S. Agency for International Development), which amounted to $664 million in 2023, has compounded an already difficult external financing environment," and that since IMF funding is often a catalyst for other official and private flows, there could be delays to World Bank and other sources of official financing.

a7000.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7000.speech: In April 2025, agreed not to disburse the remaining $126 million under Mozambique's final two reviews of its $456 million Extended Credit Facility, citing inadequate progress on policy reforms.

a7000.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7000.speech: Estimates that Mozambique's real effective exchange rate is overvalued by approximately 38%.

a7000.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a7000.speech: Announced in September 2025 the suspension of salaries for 18,000 ghost workers and a review of the wage records of another 11,000 employees, to alleviate the fiscal strain.

a7000.speaker: Mozambican government officials
a7000.speech: Expect the LNG megaprojects to generate tax revenue during the construction phase, with the government expecting to collect $483 million in LNG revenue from the Coral South and Coral North projects over 2022-2028.

a7000.speaker: Venâncio Mondlane, Mozambican opposition leader
a7000.speech: Disputed the legitimacy of the October 2024 election result and went into months of self-imposed exile; has since confirmed his new political party's intent to participate in the dialogue, despite confronting legal charges for his role in inciting post-election unrest.

a7013.speaker: China (official position)
a7013.speech: Dismisses the perception that the Asian giant has little to do with democratic governance as mere propaganda, identifying itself as a democratic system that has achieved unprecedented economic growth.

a7013.speaker: Boniface Dulani, Associate Professor and political scientist, University of Malawi
a7013.speech: Argues that China's support for the Parliament and judicial complexes is more about supporting what amplifies its presence in recipient countries. "I would not read so much into the so-called political symbolism, but what China intends to achieve. These projects are pitched and China is just responding to what is requested," he said in an interview ; "Through such infrastructure, China has penetrated space to its advantage," he argued, saying it is for the same reason the Chinese supported the construction of the African Union headquarters in Ethiopia.

a7013.speaker: Dr Michael Jana, political and international relations scholar, Wits University, South Africa
a7013.speech: Observes that China is not necessarily supporting "democratic governance from an ideological perspective". "One fundamental principle about aid is that aid is an instrument of foreign policy by the 'donor'. This principle applies whether aid is from the East or the West. This means that Chinese aid is part of its foreign policy to strengthen its international geopolitical and economic position."

a7013.speaker: Dr Michael Jana, political and international relations scholar, Wits University, South Africa
a7013.speech: Says that while Malawi has benefitted from its ties with Beijing, China has gained access to a new market, providing business and work for their labour force and industries. "The emergence of China as a donor has provided developing countries with more resources and options, has strengthened their negotiating power, and speeded up some development projects. But in international relations, that includes the aid regime. There is no free lunch."

a7013.speaker: Jimmy Kainja, media and cultural studies lecturer, University of Malawi
a7013.speech: Argues that China's actions reflect a strategic blend of development support and soft power diplomacy; says that by funding key infrastructure projects in partner countries, China signals that it is a non-conditional, constructive partner committed to state-building and institutional development. "Additionally, China's practice of prominently branding its aid as 'China Aid' serves multiple purposes. It enhances both domestic and international legitimacy, reinforces its image as a benevolent global actor, and strategically frames its assistance as pragmatic and free of ideological strings" ; "this high visibility helps foster long-term influence, potentially translating into diplomatic support and alignment with Chinese interests."

a7013.speaker: Jimmy Kainja, media and cultural studies lecturer, University of Malawi
a7013.speech: Points out that the recent announcement of US aid cut gives China an opportunity to assert its influence in aid-dependent nations.

a7013.speaker: Lu Xu, new Chinese ambassador to Malawi
a7013.speech: "The future of China-Malawi cooperation holds great promise," said at a reception held two weeks ago.

a7189.speaker: Trump administration / new US administration
a7189.speech: Revealed that USAID had financed terrorism with development aid and suspended Mali from its aid programme; in Mali, the diverted amount comes to 14 million dollars (8 billion FCFA).

a7189.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali (communique)
a7189.speech: “The ministry invites the American authorities to initiate judicial proceedings” - proceedings, the communique details, to be brought against the persons who diverted the said funds in order to finance international terrorism, notably in Mali and in the other AES (Alliance of Sahel States) countries.

a7189.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs (head of Malian diplomacy)
a7189.speech: Said Mali “recognises itself in the new orientation of the American authorities aimed at cleaning up and humanising their subsidies”; also welcomed this awareness of the reality of their “public aid”; and encouraged the actions undertaken against the subversive use of aid and its non-conformity with the essential needs of the beneficiaries.

a7189.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a7189.speech: Revealed that Mali had already refused an American grant: for the past two years the government has “refrained from signing the five-year Development Objective Grant Agreement with the United States concerning the financing of USAID projects”, and also postponed the implementation of certain activities, including those relating to social cohesion.

a7189.speaker: Government of Mali
a7189.speech: Said these measures were aimed at requiring respect for Mali's sovereignty and priorities, and at ensuring respect for national implementation procedures in matters of development aid.

a7249.speaker: Anthony G. Myers, Deputy Minister for Fiscal Affairs, Ministry of Finance and Development Planning
a7249.speech: Delivered the official opening remarks, highlighting the importance of the initiative in enhancing local financial autonomy, and emphasized that empowering counties through sound fiscal management is crucial for sustainable development: "By building the financial management capacities of our local officials, we are creating the foundation for more responsive and effective governance. Counties must be able to plan, execute, and report on their budgets independently while staying aligned with national goals." ; further urged participants to take the training seriously, noting that the success of Liberia's decentralization policy depends largely on the readiness and competence of local actors.

a7249.speaker: Prof. Alaric Tokpah, Acting Chairman of the Governance Commission
a7249.speech: Praised the MFDP and its partners for the timely initiative, and reiterated that decentralization is not merely a policy choice but a constitutional mandate that ensures citizen participation in decision-making and resource allocation: "We must continue to build synergy between central and local government institutions. Without collaboration and shared responsibility, the dream of effective decentralization will remain distant."

a7249.speaker: Representatives of development partners (European Union, SIDA, UNDP, USAID)
a7249.speech: Also addressed the gathering, each partner expressing strong commitment to Liberia's decentralization and governance reforms.

a7249.speaker: Development partner representative (unnamed)
a7249.speech: "Strong, accountable, and capable local governments are essential to achieving Liberia's long-term development goals. We are proud to be part of this capacity-building initiative that empowers local leaders to serve their communities better."

a7249.speaker: Dr. Rome D.N. Gbartea, Director of Fiscal Decentralization at MFDP
a7249.speech: Explained that the sessions are hands-on and solutions-oriented, and said the goal is to help participants apply the tools and knowledge directly in their respective counties: "This is not just theoretical knowledge. We provide tools and real-world skills that participants can apply immediately and take back with them. Our goal is to reduce waste, enhance accountability, and improve service delivery at the local level."

a7249.speaker: Participants from the four counties
a7249.speech: Welcomed the training as both timely and transformative, noting that the sessions address pressing needs around budget planning, execution, and compliance ; others emphasized the importance of replicating such training nationwide to ensure uniform capacity across all local governments.

a7249.speaker: Participant from Grand Bassa County (unnamed)
a7249.speech: "This training will help us better understand how to manage and report on our budgets and how to engage with citizens in a more transparent and responsible way."

a7315.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) July 2025 report
a7315.speech: Stated that approximately 20,000 workers in Tanzania's health sector funded by USAID, plus 30,000 health workers who received extra payments for work beyond their normal duties, will be affected by the suspension of the agency's aid ; "The suspension of foreign aid has affected the health sector across the board, that is, medical equipment, medicines and personnel. For example, USAID had employed more than 20,000 workers directly and indirectly (including civil society organisations and community actors) who were involved in services targeting diseases such as HIV/AIDS and malaria, as well as family planning and child health care services" ; "Also, approximately 30,000 health service providers who were being paid by USAID to provide additional services outside their normal duties [will likewise be affected]"

a7315.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) report
a7315.speech: Showed that Tanzania is among the nine sub-Saharan African countries that received the most USAID aid, receiving USD 400 million (about 1 trillion shillings), equal to 0.5 percent of national output in 2024 and about 40 percent of all health-sector spending, and that critical health-sector areas amounting to about 0.2 percent of national output will be affected by the suspension.

a7315.speaker: Ministry of Health of Tanzania
a7315.speech: According to the Ministry of Health, approximately 93 billion shillings was provided for the emergency plan of initial measures under the 2024/25 supplementary budget.

a7315.speaker: Jenista Mhagama, Minister of Health of Tanzania
a7315.speech: "Through the coordination of the Prime Minister's office, we have carried out a thorough assessment. We have looked at what we have, what we have ordered, and what we expect to receive. And we have already put in place a short-term, medium-term and long-term strategic plan" ; "For malaria medicines and test kits we have enough to sustain us until February 2026. For other medicines such as HIV/AIDS drugs and others, we have already taken steps. So far we have sufficient supplies to carry us through to June" ; "We have already received funds from the government under our short-term plan; we had already carried out an assessment of our needs. And we have already received 93 billion from the government. And we have already ordered medicines for all the other diseases that were being funded by those projects"

a7315.speaker: Jenista Mhagama, Minister of Health of Tanzania
a7315.speech: Also explained that, in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Service, they expect to review some of the positions that had been funded by the aid so that they can be brought under implementation plans through the government budget.

a7446.speaker: Health officials (Uganda)
a7446.speech: Noted that the deceased nurse also consulted a traditional healer.

a7446.speaker: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a7446.speech: "This is a significant step forward in enhancing pandemic preparedness and protecting lives during outbreaks. This achievement is a result of the commitment of Uganda's health workers, community involvement, and the collaborative efforts of the Ministry of Health, Makerere University, UVRI, and the extensive research network led by WHO. We appreciate the contributions of our partners, including IAVI for the vaccine donation, CEPI, EU HERA, and Canada's IDRC for their financial support, and Africa CDC for their assistance. This remarkable accomplishment would not have been possible without their collaboration."

a7446.speaker: Uganda Ministry of Health
a7446.speech: Has identified at least 234 contacts related to this outbreak.
